title: Reversible Instance Normalization for Accurate Time-Series Forecasting against Distribution Shift
key_mechanism: Reversible instance-level mean/std normalization applied at model input and denormalization at output to strip per-window shift.
notes: Foundational RevIN paper; not independently found via arXiv/OpenAlex keyword search (OpenReview-native), cited ubiquitously as baseline in all category-1/2/3 papers retrieved (e.g. Dish-TS, FAN, SAN, PADRE reference it). Confidence from consistent citation pattern across multiple verified papers.

title: Dish-TS: A General Paradigm for Alleviating Distribution Shift in Time Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Dual coefficient nets (CONET) predict distribution coefficients per input/output slice to correct intra-space and inter-space shift, generalizing RevIN.
evaluation_datasets: ETT, Electricity, Traffic, Weather, standard TSF benchmarks
notes: Also on arXiv:2302.14829.

title: Adaptive Normalization for Non-stationary Time Series Forecasting: A Temporal Slice Perspective (SAN)
key_mechanism: Slices series into temporal patches and predicts patch-level statistics (mean/std) autoregressively for normalization/denormalization, instead of one global window statistic.
notes: Title/venue confirmed via OpenAlex; abstract not retrieved.

title: Frequency Adaptive Normalization For Non-stationary Time Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Identifies and removes/re-injects dominant non-stationary Fourier components (trend+seasonal drift) instead of only first/second moments.

title: On the Role of Reversible Instance Normalization
authors_short: (2026 preprint, authors unresolved from abstract search)
key_mechanism: Analyzes when/why RevIN helps or hurts forecasting backbones.
notes: Found by arXiv keyword search only; title-only verification, not read further (outside the 5-8 closest-competitor budget).

title: Noise or Signal? Deconstructing Contradictions and An Adaptive Remedy for Reversible Normalization in Time Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Diagnoses failure modes of RevIN-style normalization and proposes an adaptive remedy.
notes: Title-only verification via arXiv search; a 2025/2026 RevIN successor confirming the normalization line is still active.

title: Learning Fast and Slow for Online Time Series Forecasting (FSNet)
key_mechanism: Slow backbone (regular backprop) + a per-layer 'fast' adapter driven by a memory of past gradients/features that reacts to recent errors; complementary learning-systems framing (slow=long-term memory, fast=short-term memory).
notes: Full text read (22pp PDF). Subsequently shown by Proceed (2024) and a concurrent ICLR'25 paper to update using (X_{t-1},Y_{t-1}), which leaks future ground truth under H-step delayed feedback -- FSNet's official reported numbers are compromised by this leakage.

title: OneNet: Enhancing Time Series Forecasting Models under Concept Drift by Online Ensembling
key_mechanism: Online convex-combination ensembling of a cross-time and a cross-variable predictor, weights updated online by a bandit-style reinforcement rule reacting to recent error.
notes: Full text read (32pp). Same information-leakage issue as FSNet per Proceed's analysis (uses X_{t-1},Y_{t-1}).

title: Proactive Model Adaptation Against Concept Drift for Online Time Series Forecasting (Proceed)
key_mechanism: Explicitly formalizes the H-step feedback delay; estimates the concept-drift direction from the last *fully observed* pair (X_{t-H},Y_{t-H}) and the current input X_t, then proactively adapts model parameters via a hypernetwork BEFORE the true label arrives, avoiding the leaky (X_{t-1},Y_{t-1}) shortcut used by FSNet/OneNet.
notes: Full text read (13pp). THE key reference for G2a: explicitly names and fixes the information-leakage bug in FSNet/OneNet's delayed-feedback handling. No gating (adapts every step), no anomaly/fault protection, no machine data.

title: Fast and Slow Streams for Online Time Series Forecasting Without Information Leakage
key_mechanism: Concurrent work to Proceed; generates pseudo-labels for the unobserved H-step horizon and concatenates with observed labels to simulate a complete, leakage-free ground truth for online updates.
evaluation_datasets: ETT, Electricity, Traffic, Weather (per Proceed's description)
notes: Not indexed in OpenAlex/arXiv/Crossref keyword search; identity confirmed via full citation (title, authors, venue, OpenReview forum ID) given in the verified Proceed full text and independently located on OpenReview. Full text not fetched (OpenReview PDF access not attempted beyond metadata) -- counts toward the 5-8 fetched-full-text budget as NOT fetched.

title: Beyond Uniform Updates: Drift Pattern Aware Online Time Series Forecasting Under Delayed Feedback (PADRE)
key_mechanism: Builds a 'Tri-View' drift representation (input context, delayed-residual trajectory, retrieved regime prototypes from an offline Pattern Bank) and computes a geometric-consistency score among the three views; a learned prompt-guided policy outputs a CONTINUOUS update gate gamma_t in (0,1) that scales the online gradient step -- large updates only when the three views agree, small/near-zero updates when residual is inconsistent (interpreted as noise/outlier/unseen mechanism).
notes: Full text read (9pp). Adopts Proceed's leakage-free H-step protocol explicitly ('We strictly adhere to the practical online forecasting protocol defined in proceed'). Closest published system to the proposed gated slow/fast design, but: (i) gate is a continuous scalar tuned for accuracy, not a hard adapt/freeze/rollback decision evaluated for 'harm', (ii) no explicit frozen-backbone-plus-adapter split -- gate scales gradient on the whole backbone, (iii) zero machine/industrial datasets, (iv) no anomaly-vs-drift ground-truth labels used to test fault-robustness.

title: Learning to Extrapolate and Adjust: Two-Stage Meta-Learning for Concept Drift in Online Time Series Forecasting (LEAF)
key_mechanism: Two meta-learned modules operating on a low-dimensional latent embedding of model parameters: an 'extrapolation' module tracks/extrapolates stable long-term ('macro') drift, and an 'adjustment' module applies a meta-learned surrogate loss for sample-specific short-term ('micro') drift; model-agnostic (MLP/RNN/CNN/Transformer).
notes: Full text read (9pp). Conceptually the closest published slow/fast (macro/micro) split for forecasting (relevant to G2c), but operates on a compressed parameter-embedding, not a literal frozen-backbone + small-adapter-state pair, has no explicit gate/arbitration rule beyond the meta-learned loss weighting, contains zero occurrences of 'delay' (does not address H-step label delay), and no machine data.

title: Delayed labelling evaluation for data streams
key_mechanism: General (non-forecasting-specific) data-stream framework and evaluation methodology (prequential variants) for the case where true labels only arrive after a delay; formalizes correct vs. leaky prequential evaluation under delay.
evaluation_datasets: synthetic and real classification data streams (not forecasting-specific)
notes: Foundational streaming-ML reference for the delayed-labelling evaluation problem generalized by Proceed/PADRE to time-series forecasting; predates and is broader than the TSF-specific line.

title: Battling the Non-stationarity in Time Series Forecasting via Test-time Adaptation (TAFAS)
key_mechanism: Test-time adapts a frozen pretrained forecaster using self-supervised feedback derived from the partially-observed horizon and a gated aggregation of multiple adaptation candidates.
notes: Full text read (15pp). Uses a gate to combine candidate predictions but is architected around test-time adaptation of a frozen forecaster rather than a persistent fast-state module; standard TSF benchmarks only, no anomaly/fault-robustness study.

title: Accurate Parameter-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Time Series Forecasting (PETSA)
key_mechanism: Keeps the pretrained forecaster fully frozen and learns small parameter-efficient (low-rank/spectral) correction modules updated online from recent errors at test time -- explicit frozen-backbone + small-adapter split.
notes: Full text read (11pp). Closest published example of the frozen-slow + small-fast-adapter split (G2c) outside PADRE/LEAF, but no H-step delay analysis, no gate for adapt/freeze/rollback decisions, no anomaly-robustness study, no machine data.

title: Towards Principled Test-Time Adaptation for Time Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Diagnoses when TSF-TTA calibration helps vs. hurts (shows adjusted predictions from stale mini-batches can be worse than the frozen model's direct prediction), then proposes Frequency-Aware Calibration (FAC), a lightweight frequency-domain correction module on top of a frozen source forecaster.
evaluation_datasets: ETT, Weather and other standard TSF benchmarks
notes: Full text read (20pp). Closest published diagnosis of 'TTA can harm forecasting accuracy' for time series (relevant to G2b) but does not use an 'adaptation harm' metric/framing, does not implement an explicit adapt/freeze/rollback gate (uses a fixed calibration architecture instead), and evaluates only on generic TSF benchmarks, not machine/industrial data.

title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting (TimesFM)
key_mechanism: Decoder-only patched-transformer pretrained on a large corpus for zero-shot forecasting.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
key_mechanism: Tokenizes scaled/quantized time series and trains a language-model (T5-style) architecture for zero-shot probabilistic forecasting.
notes: Chronos-Bolt is an efficiency-focused successor described in Amazon/AutoGluon release materials rather than a separate indexed paper; not independently verified as its own peer-reviewed publication.

title: Chronos-2: From Univariate to Universal Forecasting
key_mechanism: Extends Chronos to universal (univariate+multivariate+covariate) zero-shot forecasting.
notes: Title confirmed on arXiv; abstract not read.

title: Unified Training of Universal Time Series Forecasting Transformers (Moirai)
key_mechanism: Masked-encoder transformer with multi-patch-size projections trained on a large mixed-frequency time-series corpus (LOTSA) for zero/few-shot forecasting.

title: TiRex: Zero-Shot Forecasting Across Long and Short Horizons with Enhanced In-Context Learning
key_mechanism: xLSTM-based zero-shot time-series foundation model with in-context learning for both long and short horizons.
notes: Directly relevant to the user's own xLSTM background.

title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
key_mechanism: Extends TiRex to multivariate and streaming/online inference settings.
notes: Directly relevant: a 2026 xLSTM-based foundation model explicitly targeting streaming; a natural comparison point for G2e but not yet shown to study long-horizon machine-data drift specifically.

title: In-Context Fine-Tuning for Time-Series Foundation Models
key_mechanism: Fine-tunes a TSFM to exploit relevant examples given directly in the context window at inference time (in-context learning) rather than gradient updates.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
key_mechanism: Neural long-term memory module trained online at inference/test time via a surprise-based gradient rule with adaptive forgetting, combined with short-term (attention) memory; explicit long-term/short-term memory split framed by analogy to human memory, evaluated on language/genomics/time-series/DNA tasks, not specifically industrial forecasting.
evaluation_datasets: language modeling, common-sense reasoning, genomics, a generic time-series forecasting benchmark
notes: Full text read (27pp). Architecturally the clearest published 'long-term frozen-ish memory + fast online test-time-updated memory' design outside TSF; but (i) built for language/sequence modeling broadly, its time-series evaluation is a minor generic benchmark, not industrial data or drift-specific, (ii) no explicit gate that can veto/roll back an update when the input is a transient fault rather than genuine drift.

title: MesaNet: Sequence Modeling by Locally Optimal Test-Time Training
key_mechanism: Sequence model whose fast weights are set by a locally-optimal (least-squares) test-time training rule rather than a single gradient step.
notes: Title-only verification; general sequence-modeling paper, not forecasting- or industrial-specific.

title: Test Time Learning for Time Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Applies a test-time-training (TTT) style recurrent fast-weight update within a forecasting architecture.
notes: Direct TTT-for-TSF instance; not read at full-text depth given the fetch budget was allocated to the 8 papers above.

title: Learning Associative Inference Using Fast Weight Memory
key_mechanism: Recurrent fast-weight associative memory added on top of an LSTM controller for few-shot associative-inference tasks.
notes: Classical fast-weight-memory precedent, not forecasting-specific.

title: The role of artificial intelligence-driven soft sensors in advanced sustainable process industries: A critical review
key_mechanism: Survey of AI-driven soft-sensor design for process industries, including adaptive/online-updating soft sensors and drift-handling strategies (moving window, JIT learning, ensemble updating).
evaluation_datasets: review (no single dataset); surveys chemical/process-industry case studies
notes: Directly relevant machine/process-industry survey; the JIT-learning and moving-window soft-sensor community has practiced 'when to update' logic for over a decade, a prior body of work the thesis should engage rather than treat 'online adaptive forecasting' as novel to the deep-learning TSF community.

title: Integrating adaptive moving window and just-in-time learning paradigms for soft-sensor design
key_mechanism: Combines just-in-time (local, similarity-based) learning with an adaptive moving window whose size is itself adjusted based on detected process changes, for online soft-sensor updating.
evaluation_datasets: simulated/benchmark chemical process data (e.g. debutanizer column)

title: Multiple adaptive mechanisms for data-driven soft sensors
key_mechanism: Combines multiple concurrent adaptation mechanisms (windowing, weighting, model selection) and a meta-level arbitration for choosing which adaptation mechanism to trust at a given time.
notes: An early instance of a 'which adaptation mechanism to trust now' arbitration idea in the process-industry soft-sensor literature -- prior art relevant to G2b's gate/arbitration framing, though not for deep forecasters.

title: Soft sensor modelling by time difference, recursive partial least squares and adaptive model updating
key_mechanism: Recursive PLS soft sensor with time-difference preprocessing and an adaptive model-updating trigger.

title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
key_mechanism: Foundational survey of concept-drift detection and adaptation strategies (including 'when to adapt' triggers) for streaming predictive models in general (not forecasting-specific).
notes: Canonical background reference for the whole drift-adaptation vocabulary used across categories 2, 6, 7.

title: Learning Under Concept Drift for Regression -- A Systematic Literature Review
authors_short: Lima, de Almeida Neto, Silva Filho et al.
key_mechanism: Systematic review specifically of concept-drift handling for regression (rather than classification) streaming models.
notes: Closest existing survey to the regression/forecasting-under-drift framing of Direction 2; worth citing to show the thesis's forecasting focus is a refinement of, not a departure from, this line.
